exact_missing_items: Define `OpenSubject` in `Contracts_V0.md` with: `subject_id`; `open_intent`
Keep the intent vocabulary controlled and small: `open_source`; `open_preview`; `open_review`
Keep resolver-support metadata out of the contract.

State the resolution rule directly: `OpenSubject(subject_id = doc:...)` resolves to workspace-backed source opening; `OpenSubject(subject_id = artifact:...)` resolves to real document source if one exists; otherwise it resolves to transient `generated://<artifact_id>` source opening

`OpenSubject` does not carry: `project_id`, `thread_id`, `run_id`, `tab_id`, `panel_id`, `inspector_target`, `origin_surface`, `source_kind`, `backing_document_id`, `last_saved_path`, `generated://<artifact_id>`, preview persistence state, transport mode
Formalize the three-way command taxonomy: pure shell/view-state commands; route-consuming navigation commands; domain mutation/runtime commands
Keep `cmd.panel.switch` and `cmd.source_control.switch_subview` as pure shell/view-state commands with controlled destination vocabularies.
Move object-targeting payload semantics out of `cmd.panel.switch` and into canonical route-consuming commands or normalized `route_target` wrappers.

Treat `cmd.chat.open_thread_usage`, `cmd.chat.focus_thread_usage`, `cmd.project.open`, `cmd.artifacts.show_in_*`, and cross-surface Orchestrator pivots as wrapper navigation commands over canonical route targeting rather than as generic layout toggles.
The contract now has enough shape to define concrete route normalization for the most common user-facing flows.

cost usage -> Show in Usage: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=usage_event`, `object_id=<canonical usage event id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread-scoped, `inspector_target=usage`
cost usage -> Show in Ledger: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=usage_event`, `object_id=<id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread-scoped, `tab_id=ledger`

wizard resume: `target_kind=primary_view`, `project_id=<id>`, `object_kind=wizard`, `object_id=<wizard_id>`, `thread_id=<id>` when thread must be restored; serialized `resume_url` carries narrow step anchor detail
chat search hit: `target_kind=side_panel`, `project_id=<id>`, `thread_id=<id>`, `object_kind=message`, `object_id=<message_id>`

node detail pivot: `target_kind=page_tab`, `project_id=<id>`, `focused_run_id=<run_id>`, `object_kind=node`, `object_id=<node_id>`, `tab_id=node_graph`, `inspector_target=details|evidence|usage|history`

route activation overrides remembered state only when required to satisfy the requested destination/object/context; otherwise it should reuse persisted shell state and local destination defaults

MUST override: target object identity; destination surface when the action explicitly names a different surface; scope required to make the target meaningful (project_id, thread_id, focused_run_id, or an explicitly requested panel/tab)
MUST NOT reuse persisted state when doing so would: land on the wrong object; hide the requested target behind the wrong tab/subview; silently keep the user on a stale run/thread/project context
Add a shared route-activation override rule in the contract/GUI owner docs.
